title: Plastic to apparel: an analysis of sustainable purchasing intention using a machine learning ensemble
authors: Cabrera, C.A.L.; Ong, A.K.S.; Diaz, J.F.T.; Gumasing, M.J.J.; Cahigas, M.M.L.
tldr: Machine learning ensemble of RFC and ANN predicts Filipino consumers' purchasing intention for sustainable plastic-derived apparel, with customer perceived value and perceived behavioral control as primary drivers.
problem_and_motivation: Despite the proliferation of recycled and upcycled sustainable fashion products, there remains a significant gap in understanding the sustainable purchasing behavior of consumers, particularly in developing countries like the Philippines.
approach: The study developed a Sustainability Theory of Planned Behavior (STPB) model integrating five sustainability domains with TPB constructs.
Data were collected from 500 valid Filipino respondents through a structured questionnaire.
Random Forest Classifier (RFC) and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) were employed as machine learning classifiers.
Data preprocessing included feature selection, correlation analysis, data cleaning, and aggregation.
Iterative hyperparameter tuning was performed with 70/30 train-test split and 10-fold cross-validation.
findings: num: RFC achieved 92% classification accuracy in predicting behavioral intention toward sustainable apparel.
num: ANN achieved 91% accuracy at 150 epochs under 30 hidden layer nodes.
Customer perceived value and perceived behavioral control were the primary factors influencing behavioral intention.
Attitude, subjective norm, perceived authority support, and perceived economic and environmental concerns also contributed significantly.
RFC outperformed ANN and other classifiers including decision trees, SVM, and KNN across accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 metrics.

definitions.definition: Theory of Planned Behavior, a framework measuring behavioral characteristics through social and psychological constructs.
Sustainability Theory of Planned Behavior, the extended model integrating sustainability domains with TPB constructs.
Random Forest Classifier, an ensemble machine learning method using multiple decision trees for classification.
Artificial Neural Network, a computational model inspired by biological neural networks for pattern recognition.
Customer Perceived Value, the consumer's overall assessment of the utility of a product.
Perceived Behavioral Control, the perceived ease or difficulty of performing a particular behavior.

limitations: Study limited to sustainable fashion domain and Filipino respondents only.
Self-reported survey data may suffer from social desirability and common method bias.

remember_this: RFC achieved 92% accuracy classifying sustainable purchase intentions from survey data.
Customer perceived value and perceived behavioral control were the strongest predictors of purchasing intention.
The STPB framework integrates five sustainability domains with Theory of Planned Behavior constructs.
ANN and RFC significantly outperformed SVM, KNN, and decision tree baselines.
Machine learning ensemble methods effectively predict behavioral intentions from Likert-scale survey data.
